scope: Extend existing Supabase Auth with email password recovery, Google OAuth UI, and optional contact phone collection with a one-time skippable prompt for accounts without a number.

keep: Supabase Auth, existing GitHub OAuth, server-side profile setup gates, backend profile ownership
extend: Add Google provider button using existing callback
Add password reset request and update forms
Add private contact phone capture and self-service update

schemaImpact.rollout: Apply the additive optional-prompt migration before deploying frontend/backend. Accounts with no phone see a one-time prompt that can be skipped. No NOT NULL backfill or phone-login capability is introduced.
schemaImpact.rollback: Revert frontend/backend prompt changes first. Retain the additive contact_phone and prompt-dismissal columns and functions until a separate reviewed cleanup; do not drop collected numbers on rollback.

auth.description: Password recovery uses Supabase emailed recovery links; Google OAuth uses existing callback; phone does not authenticate.

tenant.description: Contact RPC reads/writes only auth.uid(); profile API remains owner-bound. Contact column has no public select/update grant.

approval.description: No external app approval flow changes.

credentials.description: Google provider needs an enabled Supabase OAuth configuration; no client secret is committed or read.

egress.description: Recovery requests use the existing Supabase Auth endpoint and transactional email provider.

cost.description: Recovery emails may consume the existing Supabase email quota; no new purchased service is enabled.

billing.description: No billing or payment behavior changes.

tests.scope: Contact number normalization and existing auth presentation/timing tests
OAuth callback rejects external and malformed return targets
Existing signup, provider-error and auth-lookup contracts remain aligned with contact and recovery routes

architecture.reason: Reuses Supabase Auth, private profile SQL, and current Next layouts; no new identity provider or scheduler.

rollout: Release Google OAuth and the optional, unverified contact-phone prompt after CI and authenticated preview checks. Keep password recovery hidden by default; enable NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_RECOVERY_ENABLED only after production custom SMTP and a recovery-link test succeed.
rollback: Revert the app revision and keep the additive column; disable Google provider if it was enabled; retain the prior auth flow and avoid deleting user data.
knownGaps: Password recovery remains hidden until production custom SMTP and a recovery-link test succeed
Contact numbers are optional and unverified by design; they are not used for login
The signed-in preview skip journey passed, but contact-number submission and reset-link password change remain unverified
PR frontend/backend changes are not deployed to default production traffic
placeholderClaimsRemaining: This code is not a live verified authentication journey until signed-in staging and email/OAuth callbacks pass

blockers: CI/review and app deployment for the Google and optional-contact release
Production-grade SMTP and reset-link test before enabling password recovery
